content: Canvas excels with hundreds+ of animated objects (pixel-level compositing, no per-node DOM/accessibility overhead) but requires manual hit-testing/accessibility. SVG is DOM-resident (each shape a real element), CSS-styleable, has built-in accessibility (ARIA), and is more performant than Canvas for small-to-moderate object counts over a large surface, but degrades as element count climbs into the thousands. DOM+CSS is best for small counts of richly-interactive, text-heavy elements. For a board with ~40-60 discrete pieces (boat, ~6 crossing marbles, 4 dice, track beats, player panels) SVG or DOM+CSS both fit comfortably; Canvas is unnecessary at this scale and would sacrifice CSS styling / built-in accessibility / easy click-target wiring for no real perf gain.
